title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
notes: Read live on 2026-11-21 (curl GET, HTTP 200 at 07:05Z UTC; openai.com answered plain requests that day). The live post says Wallet was built in partnership with American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa. The launch-day text, in the Internet Archive capture of 2026-11-13T16:04:07Z (archiveUrl, read 2026-11-14 while openai.com refused automated reads), named American Express, Mastercard and Visa. OpenAI did not mark the change: the page data carries only the publication date (2026-11-13), and the RSS item (pubDate 2026-11-13T15:00:00Z) is unchanged. Chase appears only in the partner sentence; the quote carousel still has three entries, from American Express (Luke Gebb, who calls Wallet the first American Express Agentic Commerce Experiences integration), Mastercard and Visa. The rest matches the capture: Wallet is initially available through dots for ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US aged 18 and older with eligible US-issued cards and begins rolling out that day; the user adds a card once, reviews the items, total and selected card before each purchase and approves with a security check such as Face ID or a fingerprint scan, and each approval creates a record of the authorized purchase; after approval the payment network provides a payment token with a card number, security code and expiration date, so neither the business nor the agent sees the actual card details; users keep card rewards and protections for eligible disputes, and businesses keep pricing, fulfillment, returns and customer service; fraud prevention partners include Forter, Riskified, Sardine and Signifyd and PSPs include Adyen, Checkout.com and Stripe (lists marked as not exhaustive); risk systems may still decline legitimate agent purchases; ChatGPT has 1.2B weekly users; delegation within spending limits, categories or time periods is described as a future expectation without a date. As read 2026-11-21 the post also says websites can add WebMCP tools; when that sentence appeared is not known. It states no fee and never mentions the Agentic Commerce Protocol, ACP, Instant Checkout, Delegate Payment or Shared Payment Tokens. Its meta, og and twitter descriptions, like OpenAI's RSS description (src-openai-news-rss-20261114, src-openai-acp-news-rss-20261121), still name agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex and dots; the post body names dots only, and OpenAI's help article says Wallet works only in conversations with a dot (src-openai-wallet-help-purchases).

title: Accept payments (Commerce in ChatGPT, OpenAI developer docs)
notes: Read through the .md twin (HTTP 200 at 2026-11-15T02:47Z UTC). Customers can pay with ChatGPT Wallet on the business's website or use a payment method already saved there, after approving in ChatGPT; the business handles the order, fulfillment, customer support and fraud decisions. Wallet works with existing checkout pages and payment forms, with no Wallet-specific integration. The merchant receives a network token instead of the card number and can use the Payment Account Reference (PAR) to link it to the account; the customer consents only to the specific transaction, so the credential must not be reused or saved for another purchase; subscriptions work if the checkout supports recurring billing, with the customer's consent and the processor's practice for merchant-initiated transactions; Wallet is a separate option beside an existing card-on-file flow. OpenAI says it is rolling out user signals in the Forwarded HTTP header with the parameters asn, for, ip-country, ip-prefix, locale, tz and user-agent, and that the signals may vary during the rollout. First archive capture of the page 2026-11-13T17:12:22Z. Re-read 2026-11-21 (HTTP 200 at 07:07Z UTC): unchanged on these points, and the page says its guidance and the cloud browser access checks are optional steps that can help Wallet work smoothly.

title: Help ensure cloud browser access to your site (Commerce in ChatGPT, OpenAI developer docs)
notes: Read through the .md twin (9,847 bytes, HTTP 200 at 2026-11-21T07:07Z UTC); the page has no date. It says a firewall may block or interrupt cloud browser visits made on a user's behalf and, to help those requests go through reliably, tells sites to add ChatGPT's agent profile to the firewall's allowlist while keeping other security controls in place; a site that applies an allowlist exception for signed browser requests should verify their signatures first. Its FAQ says an allowlist rule for verified cloud browser visits does not change how the site handles other traffic and that an exception can apply site-wide. Akamai, Cloudflare, HUMAN and Vercel verify the signatures automatically. Provider identifiers: Akamai lists the traffic as ChatGPT Agent in its AI Fetchers and Agents category; Cloudflare shows dots, OpenAI under Personal Agents or, for WAF custom rules, bot tag chatgpt-agent and detection ID 129220581, found by searching for ChatGPT Operator; HUMAN lists ChatGPT Agent in Sightline Known Bots & Crawlers and under AgenticTrust AI Agents Permissions; Vercel recognizes the ChatGPT Agent entry, identified as chatgpt-operator, and a Vercel-hosted site whose rules do not block the traffic needs no additional configuration. ChatGPT uses Web Bot Auth (RFC 9421 HTTP Message Signatures) to identify certain cloud browser requests, not web crawlers: a signed request carries Signature and Signature-Input headers and a Signature-Agent header set to the quoted string https://chatgpt.com, and keys are published at https://chatgpt.com/.well-known/http-message-signatures-directory. FAQ: site owners cannot yet control which actions users take, but OpenAI requires human review before any consequential action across all users; browser access needs no product feed or plugin; OpenAI says customers are ultimately responsible for the actions they take, so support follows the business's normal process. The page does not say whether the signature covers the Forwarded header. This record's note of the 2026-11-14 read said the cloud browser needs no allowlist, and that was right when read: the page's Internet Archive captures of 2026-11-14T13:37:10Z and 2026-11-15T16:07:26Z (same digest, read 2026-11-21) still say a site does not need to add the cloud browser to an allowlist, so OpenAI changed the page after 2026-11-15T16:07Z and gives no date for the change.

title: Build a plugin (Commerce in ChatGPT, OpenAI developer docs)
notes: Read through the .md twin (2026-11-15T02:47Z UTC). Recommends a headless MCP plugin and says iframe-based MCP UI is not supported in dots; the tool groups for product lookup, carts, checkout and order history (when supported) are examples, not mandatory tool names or a universal schema; product lookup and carts should work in guest mode; OpenAI supports mutual TLS for MCP servers; a plugin that cannot finish checkout returns a continue_url browser handoff, ideally a short-lived one-time authenticated link. Its reference checkout shape for create_checkout, get_checkout and update_checkout is described as following a cart and checkout proposal that the page does not name; its fields (item id, title and price; totals with only type and amount; a message with severity requires_buyer_input and a path; status requires_escalation) match UCP's checkout schema, not ACP 2026-04-17's. Its cart and product lookup examples are OpenAI's own. OpenAI says it is still working on interaction patterns between third-party plugins and ChatGPT Wallet.

title: Position of the Council at first reading on the Payment Services Regulation (ST 8543/1/26 REV 1)
notes: Dated 2026-11-04 (Brussels) and marked adopted by the Council on 2026-10-29 (procedure 2023/0210(COD)). No AI-agent provision: no hit for agentic, AI agent or autonomous. Recital 170: a pass-through wallet operator that verifies strong customer authentication needs an outsourcing agreement with the payer's PSP, which keeps full liability for the operator's failures to apply it; recitals 16 and 171: technical service providers and payment scheme operators are liable, up to the transaction amount, for failing to support strong customer authentication. Entry into force 20 days after publication, application 21 months later (Article 124). The Legislative Observatory lists the file as awaiting Parliament's second reading, with an indicative plenary date of 2026-12-14 (read 2026-11-14).

title: Commerce policies
notes: Read with curl GET, HTTP 200 at 2026-11-21T07:05Z UTC; the page shows 'Updated: September 29, 2026'. The policies set eligibility standards for product listings and merchant participation in OpenAI's shopping experiences, on top of the Usage policies and applicable law. Prohibited products and services include pornography, adult sexual products and gambling services; illegal or regulated drugs, drug paraphernalia, prescription-only medications or medical products, and supplements; counterfeit, stolen and other illicit goods; malware and covert surveillance; alcoholic beverages over 0.5% ABV or kits enabling distillation, and tobacco and nicotine products and their consumption accessories; firearms, ammunition, explosives, illegal or age-restricted weapons and self-defense weapons; recalled or unsafe products; and fake IDs, personal data lists and social media manipulation. They also bar products commonly restricted by payment networks, such as debt relief and credit repair, crypto and NFTs, and travel services with high chargeback risk such as charter flights, timeshares and cruise tickets, as well as high-risk digital entitlements such as in-game currency.

title: Making purchases with ChatGPT Wallet
notes: Read with curl GET, HTTP 200 at 2026-11-21T07:05Z UTC. The page data gives updatedAt 2026-11-19T23:24:49Z (the page shows 'Updated: yesterday'); no first-publication date is shown. Availability: Wallet is rolling out gradually to eligible ChatGPT Pro users in the US; it works in conversations with a dot, the user sets up a dot first, and it is not available in Chat, Work or standalone Codex threads; approving a purchase requires biometric verification, such as Face ID or Touch ID, on a supported device. Cards: eligible US-issued American Express, Chase, Mastercard and Visa cards; the user must be 18 or older, live in the US and have a US billing address for the card; only the primary cardholder can add an eligible Chase card, not an authorized user, and the user approves the connection in the Chase mobile app, scanning a QR code when starting on a computer; the bank may ask to verify the card during setup with a code or an approval in its app; some US-issued debit cards are supported, but Chase debit cards are not; virtual cards cannot be added at launch, which is separate from the virtual card number Wallet uses for an approved purchase. Purchases: after approval the dot uses a virtual card number linked to the selected card, so the number entered at checkout may differ from the physical card, and the FAQ says Wallet generates a payment token for each use; if the user agrees to a recurring or continuous payment plan, the merchant may store the credential and charge it again under those terms; 'Ready to check out' means the approval is complete and does not confirm that the merchant placed the order; Wallet may not complete checkout at every store. Help: the merchant handles order status, cancellations, returns and refunds; the card issuer handles declined, pending, disputed or unrecognized charges and bank verification problems; OpenAI Support handles Wallet errors, suspected account access and purchases that differ from what the user approved.
